title: Los Angeles in 1942: Central Avenue clubs and swampy Watts
summary: Bigard names the Cotton Club and Club Alabam on Central Avenue, remembers Watts as swampland where he went crawfishing, and says after-hours spots there were mostly hustling for rent.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: When you left the band in 1942 and here I'm came to Los Angeles, what was going on musically here? I think you said there were what, two big clubs? The Cotton Club --
The Cotton Club and -- on Central Avenue.
-- Alabam, Club Alabam. Then they had some outskirts -- clubs out on, like, in Watts and all that, before Watts was Watt's.
But the first name I knew it, what they called it was Nigger Slough.
Slough, S-l-o-u-g-h, you know, like that tune that Rex made, --
Yeah. And I used to go crawfishing out there and --
-- get those little bugs, you know, mud bugs, and pick them off the ground. It was all swampland back there.
Sure, it was swampland when I got here.
And what -- I think your wife was saying there were after-hours spots in Watts?
And there was after-hours spots, yeah. There were a lot of after-hours spots but that was all that was hanging around.
They were hustling people, I mean, to get the rent paid or --
